_comment: ⚠ THE ONE AXIS ON WHICH THE TWO cmdguard IMPLEMENTATIONS DO NOT AGREE, AND THE SHARED
CORPUS CANNOT SAY SO. cmdguard-pure.ts's header states the contract this repository runs
on: "THIS IS A PORT ... Two guards that disagree are worse than one, because the weaker
one is the one that matters ... a drift fails a build." cmdguard-corpus.json is what makes
that true — but a corpusCase carries ONE `decision` field for BOTH implementations, so it
can only ever record a verdict the two already share. It is structurally unable to express
a drift; it can only express a settled answer. That is why this file exists beside it.
MEASURED, NOT READ (W4.34, tab-h4w7): Go trims with strings.TrimSpace (unicode.IsSpace) and
TypeScript with String.prototype.trim (WhiteSpace + LineTerminator). Those two sets are not
the same set. They differ on exactly two code points, and the ports differ with them:
U+0085 NEXT LINE                 Go strips it, JS does not  -> Go allows, TS confirms
U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE JS strips it, Go does not  -> TS allows, Go confirms
Neither is an escalation to an arbitrary command: the head still has to be in the allowlist,
and both call sites treat `confirm` as a prompt rather than a block. What it costs is that
one side runs unattended what the other stops to ask about — on a boundary whose own header
says two guards that disagree are worse than one.
⚠ WHICH WAY TO CONVERGE IS A PERMISSION DECISION AND THIS FILE DOES NOT TAKE IT. Matching Go
widens the extension on U+0085; matching JS widens the agent on U+FEFF; trimming neither
narrows both and widens nothing, which is the only direction that adds no permission. That
is a call for Nicolai, and W4.34's own scope discipline pre-committed to reporting it.
⚠ WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR IN THE MEANTIME: it makes the drift FAIL A BUILD, which is what the
header already claimed. Every verdict below is measured from the shipped code, and both
suites assert their own side against it AND assert that the set of divergent code points is
EXACTLY the two named. A third divergence reds. A fixed divergence reds too, and the failure
message says so — the day someone takes the decision, this file is what tells them to delete
the entry rather than a stale opinion sitting here forever.
⚠ HOW TO REGENERATE, DESCRIBED RATHER THAN POINTED AT: every `go`/`ts` verdict below is
the output of running the command through agent/internal/cmdguard.Check and through
extension/src/agent/cmdguard-pure.check respectively, and `agree` is the two compared on
decision AND reason. `cases` is the cross of the code points above — the union of Go's
unicode.White_Space and ECMAScript's WhiteSpace+LineTerminator, plus three near-miss
characters neither strips — with six shapes that place the character where a trim runs:
leading, trailing, surrounding, after-semicolon, after-pipe, interior. Regenerating means
re-running both guards over that cross; it is deliberately not a script path here, because
a pointer at one machine's home directory is not something a reader can check.
